payload.acceptance_criteria: init wires a post-merge hook that folds every shard into the trunk log; it merges into an existing hook rather than replacing it, honours core.hooksPath, and uninstall removes exactly the block it wrote and nothing else. A repository whose hook the kit did not write is left alone and said so.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a team installs only the tracker kit and lands branches for a year, I want their shards folded into the trunk without anyone running a command, so I can keep the merge promise from decaying into a directory nobody can git add.

Sharding landed in basicly-v5zvsh1 and the engine got its automatic compaction in basicly-62gd7je. A consumer with no engine has neither: compact is a command someone must remember, and fsck only warns above 1000 shards, so the first alarm comes about a year in. Measured on this repository, 8.2 merges a day is 3000 shards a year, and one git add over 10000 files costs 35.59s on NTFS against 0.66s on ext4 with the ratio doubling every decade.

Measured 2026-09-18 rather than recalled: a post-merge hook fires on a fast-forward pull and on a no-fast-forward merge, both. So a developer pulling the trunk after someone else's branch landed is exactly the moment the shard becomes foldable, and the hook is the right one.

Two problems the tier kit's hook installer did not face. A repository may point core.hooksPath somewhere other than .git/hooks, and writing the wrong place would leave a hook nothing runs. And a hook file may already exist and belong to pre-commit or husky, so it must be merged into rather than clobbered.
payload.requirements: no engine import, standard library only, no subprocess, Python 3.9 floor. The hook body carries no absolute path, no username and no bare python3, because a bare python3 on Windows hits an execution alias. core.hooksPath is read from .git/config as a file, which is the same boundary SPEC section 4.0 already amended for .git/HEAD.
payload.title: compact a standalone consumer's shards without them remembering
